 Can Aggies cure road woes?
 Published 5:15 am Friday, November 6, 2026
 By Lane Fobbs 
 The Texas A&M Aggies will hit the road for a Saturday afternoon battle against the No. 21 South Carolina Gamecocks. (File Photo) 
 Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... 
 On the SEC coaches call last week, Texas A&M head coach Mike Elko said he still believes that quarterback Marcel Reed gives the Aggies the best chance to win.  
 The third-year starter is at or near the bottom of all major passing categories in the SEC and his eight interceptions thrown leads the conference. It has led to loud corners of the A&M fanbase to pine for backup quarterback Brady Hart to see the field.  
 The 6-foot-4, 200-pound Hart has thrown for 143 yards, a pair of touchdowns and one interception over his limited mop-up work. Elko intimated he is open to the idea of inserting Hart, as soon as his checkpoints are met.  
 “Brady gets a ton of opportunities to showcase where he’s at,” said Elko. “He’s had a ton of opportunities to show us whether or not he’s ready to step in and be the guy. The challenge to him has been if you want opportunities there’s a level we need to see in order to feel comfortable about doing that.” 
 Indeed there is a higher level A&M’s entire roster must attain as the Aggies hit the road for a game at No. 21 South Carolina (5-3, 3-3), Saturday at 2 p.m. Texas A&M’s last road win came on Nov. 8 of last season-a 38-17 win at unranked Missouri.  
 The Gamecocks stumbled out to an 0-3 start to kickoff SEC play, but have since reeled off three straight victories, the most recent of which, a 27-24 home victory over then-No.11 Tennessee. Powering their resurgence is junior quarterback LaNorris Sellers.

 The 6-foot-3, 238-pound Seller is a tank in the build of Dante Culpepper, Steve McNair, and Cam Newton. Seller is able to hurt defenses with his sheer size and ability to place the ball neatly where receivers need it to be. This year, Sellers has the fourth-most passing yards in the SEC with 1,849, to go along with 16 touchdowns and seven interceptions. He also ranks fifth in the SEC in rushing yards with 603 yards and six total touchdowns. The entire offense seems to be learning from the growing pains under new offensive coordinator Kendall Briles.  
 “He’s playing at an elite level,” said Elko, when asked about Sellers. “We know he’s just improved tremendously over the last three weeks. They do a really good job of staying third and manageable.” 
 Saturday’s game comes amid a once promising year that needed just eight weeks to dissipate into the gentle autumn winds of early November. Texas A&M’s Nov. 14 home game against Tennessee, where the crowd has been asked to wear dark for a night game, was instead moved from primetime to an afternoon spot to be decided this week.  
 Texas A&M was nowhere near the top 12 teams in the country that heard their name called during Tuesday’s first reveal of the College Football Playoff rankings. With a mediocre record, the Aggies now take questions of whether or not the team is motivated instead of whether or not they think it should be in the postseason.   
 Texas A&M freshman running back KJ Edwards has already lost more games than he did during his entire tenure as the centerpiece of a Carthage High School offense that won three UIL 3A State Championships. Edwards leads all Aggies in rushing with 360 total yards on 55 attempts. The losses have been high, but Edwards says A&M’s resolve has been the same.  
 “This November is about how we respond and it starts this week,” said Edwards.
